pairs.title: Greenhouse vent and the heater
pairs.version_a: Ines asked her neighbour Tomas to look after her greenhouse while she was away for a week. Her one firm instruction was to close the roof vent every evening, because her tomato seedlings cannot survive a cold night. On Thursday Tomas watched a football match, forgot about the vent and went to bed. He knew nothing else about the state of the greenhouse that night. The temperature dropped below freezing, and by morning all two hundred seedlings were dead. A gardener who examined the greenhouse afterwards found that the heater had worked normally all through that night. She concluded that with the vent closed the greenhouse would have stayed warm enough, and the seedlings would have lived.
pairs.version_b: Ines asked her neighbour Tomas to look after her greenhouse while she was away for a week. Her one firm instruction was to close the roof vent every evening, because her tomato seedlings cannot survive a cold night. On Thursday Tomas watched a football match, forgot about the vent and went to bed. He knew nothing else about the state of the greenhouse that night. The temperature dropped below freezing, and by morning all two hundred seedlings were dead. A gardener who examined the greenhouse afterwards found that the heater had broken down early that evening. She concluded that even with the vent closed the greenhouse would have got too cold, and the seedlings would have died anyway.
pairs.intended_difference: In A the seedlings would have lived had Tomas closed the vent (heater worked); in B they would have died anyway because the heater broke down, unknown to him.
pairs.judgment_question: How much is Tomas responsible for Ines losing her seedlings?
pairs.comprehension_question: What did the gardener find out about the greenhouse heater on that night?
pairs.option_a: It had worked normally all night
pairs.option_b: It had broken down early that evening
pairs.prediction_rationale: Readers hold Tomas nearly fully responsible when closing the vent would have saved the seedlings, but mark him down clearly when the loss was coming regardless, even though his lapse is identical.
pairs.originality_note: An everyday house-sitting lapse with a hidden equipment failure, not a version of any standard overdetermination case such as two shooters or poisoned canteens.

pairs.title: Heater in the village hall kitchen
pairs.version_a: A village hall has a rule: electric heaters must never be plugged into the kitchen sockets, because the kitchen wiring is old. Dana, a new volunteer, was told about this rule at her induction and remembered it. One cold Saturday she plugged a heater into a kitchen socket to warm her feet while she sorted donations. A few minutes later the caterer, Lev, switched on the big tea urn in the kitchen, as he is allowed to do. The heater and the urn together overloaded the circuit, and the power to the kitchen cut out. Nobody noticed, and the food bank's freezer stayed off all weekend. On Monday, sixty kilos of frozen food had to be thrown away.
pairs.version_b: A village hall has a rule: electric heaters must never be plugged into the kitchen sockets, because the kitchen wiring is old. Dana, a new volunteer, was never told about this rule, and no sign mentioned it. One cold Saturday she plugged a heater into a kitchen socket to warm her feet while she sorted donations. A few minutes later the caterer, Lev, switched on the big tea urn in the kitchen, as he is allowed to do. The heater and the urn together overloaded the circuit, and the power to the kitchen cut out. Nobody noticed, and the food bank's freezer stayed off all weekend. On Monday, sixty kilos of frozen food had to be thrown away.
pairs.intended_difference: In A Dana had been told the rule and remembered it; in B she had never been told and no sign mentioned it.
pairs.judgment_question: How much did Dana cause the frozen food to be lost?
pairs.scale_label_1: Did not cause it at all
pairs.comprehension_question: Before that Saturday, had Dana been told about the rule on heaters in the kitchen?
pairs.option_a: Yes, she was told at her induction
pairs.option_c: The hall had no rule about heaters
pairs.prediction_rationale: People tend to rate a knowing rule-breaker as more of a cause than an unknowing one, but since her physical contribution is identical the shift should be modest.
pairs.originality_note: A new setting (overloaded circuit, spoiled food-bank freezer) with a permitted second contributor, not the pen-taking professor or shared-computer cases.

pairs.title: Tiles thrown onto the side path
pairs.version_a: Karl was replacing tiles on the roof of a two-storey house. To save time, he threw the old tiles down onto the side path instead of carrying them down the ladder. He knew that the downstairs tenant, Mrs Abel, occasionally used that path to reach the bins, though on most days nobody did. He had not put up a barrier or a warning. He could not see the path from where he worked, so he threw each tile without looking. At around three o'clock Mrs Abel stepped onto the path with a bag of rubbish at the moment a tile came down. It struck her shoulder and broke her collarbone. She needed an operation and was off work for two months.
pairs.version_b: Karl was replacing tiles on the roof of a two-storey house. To save time, he threw the old tiles down onto the side path instead of carrying them down the ladder. He knew that the downstairs tenant, Mrs Abel, occasionally used that path to reach the bins, though on most days nobody did. He had not put up a barrier or a warning. He could not see the path from where he worked, so he threw each tile without looking. At around three o'clock Mrs Abel stepped onto the path with a bag of rubbish a moment after a tile came down. It had landed a step ahead of her and she was unhurt. She dropped her rubbish in the bin and went back indoors.
pairs.intended_difference: In A a tile happens to hit Mrs Abel and breaks her collarbone; in B, by a moment's difference in timing, the tile misses and she is unhurt.
pairs.judgment_question: How wrong was Karl's choice to throw the tiles down onto the path?
pairs.comprehension_question: What happened to Mrs Abel when she stepped onto the path?
pairs.option_a: A tile hit her and broke her collarbone
pairs.option_b: A tile landed ahead of her and she was unhurt
pairs.option_c: She saw the tiles falling and stayed indoors
pairs.prediction_rationale: The choice is clearly careless in both versions so ratings start high, but an actual injury usually pushes wrongness ratings up by roughly a point over a near miss.
pairs.originality_note: A roofer's shortcut with a split-second timing difference, unlike the familiar drunk-driver, bath-drowning or negligent-parent luck cases.
